title: Affordable Oxygen Microscopy-Assisted Biofabrication of Multicellular Spheroids
protocol: Prepare all sterile materials and instruments by autoclaving or filter sterilization.
Clean recyclable PDMS stamps from agarose and store them aseptically in 70% ethanol at least 1 day prior to spheroid generation.
Transfer micro-patterned PDMS stamps from a storage vial to a sterile Petri dish.
Air-dry the stamps with the smooth surface up under sterile laminar airflow conditions for 10 min.
Place each stamp with a micro-patterned surface up in the middle of the well of a 12-well sterile tissue culture plate.
Air dry the plates for 1-2 min with an open lid to ensure excess liquid evaporates completely.
Weigh 1.5 g of agarose into a clean glass bottle.
Add 50 mL of sterile distilled water to the agarose and cover the bottle with a lid.
Melt the mixture in a microwave to make 50 mL of 3% homogeneous agarose solution.
Handle hot agarose solution with caution to avoid splashing and potential burns.
Add ~2 mL of hot agarose solution immediately to each well of the 12-well cell culture plates using a sterile serological pipette, ensuring it completely covers the PDMS stamp.
Incubate the plate under sterile air-flow for 20 min with the lid opened to allow agarose to solidify.
Turn the agarose layer upside down in each well carefully with a sterile small spatula to detach and remove the PDMS stamp smoothly from the top surface of the agarose layer.
Add ~200 µL of sterile water on the smooth topside of the stamp, gently detach it from the agarose using a spatula, ensuring no damage to the microwells.
Remove the PDMS stamp carefully from each well without damaging the microwell structures.
Add 1 mL of corresponding sterile cell culture media to the agarose stamps for direct use in each well.
Cover the plate with the lid and incubate overnight at 4 °C.
Use PBS solution instead of medium for long-term storage (up to 2 weeks at 4 °C).
Avoid letting the agarose dry during storage.
Warm the agarose micro-patterned plates for 1 h at 37 °C in a CO2 incubator before use.
Prepare α-minimal essential medium (MEM) supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS).
Supplement growth factors in endothelial cell growth medium 2 for HUVEC cultivation.
Prepare heterocellular spheroid growth medium by mixing HUVEC and hDPSC growth media in a 1:1 ratio.
Rinse 70%-90% confluent cell culture with prewarmed (37 °C) PBS (10 mL per 75 cm2 flask).
Add dissociating enzyme solution (0.05% trypsin and 1 mM EDTA; 1 mL per 75 cm2 flask) to the cell culture.
Incubate for 3-5 min at 37 °C in 5% CO2, 95% humidity.
Neutralize trypsin with complete cell culture media containing 10% FBS (5 mL of media per 1 mL of dissociation solution).
For HUVEC cultured in a low FBS medium, add 0.5 mL of 100% FBS to the trypsin-treated cell culture.
Centrifuge to transfer cells to their growth medium.
Dissociate cell aggregates by pipetting using a 1000 μL pipette tip on the top of a 10 mL serological pipette to obtain single-cell suspension.
Count the number of cells per 1 mL of the cell suspension.
Dilute the cell suspension to 500,000 cells per mL.
For heterocellular hDPSC / HUVEC in a 1:1 spheroid ratio, add equal volumes of corresponding cell suspensions to have a final cell concentration of 500,000 cells per mL.
Add concentrated O2 probe solution (nanoparticles, 1 mg/mL stock) to the prepared cell suspension to a final concentration of 5 μg/mL.
Exchange 1 mL of old media in a micropatterned well for 1 mL of the prepared cell suspension (500,000 cells per 1 mL, with 5 μg/mL O2 probe).
Culture spheroids in CO2 incubator for 2-5 days in continuous presence of the O2 probe.
Add 0.2-0.5 mL of culture media carefully to avoid disturbing spheroids if required.
Exchange growth media with fresh one without the probe after spheroid formation.
Monitor signals from the preserved probe staining in generated spheroids for long-term monitoring.
Prepare a 10% (w/v) GelMA solution in medium under a laminar air-flow.
Weigh 0.2 g of sterile GelMA with a degree of substitution of 78 in a 15 mL tube.
Add 1.9 mL of α-MEM to the GelMA and let it dissolve by mixing on a rotary shaker at 37 °C for about 2 hours.
Resuspend spheroids in micropatterned wells by pipetting and collect them in a 15 mL tube.
Perform an additional rinse with PBS to ensure all spheroids are collected from the agarose microwells.
Avoid touching or damaging the agarose microwells during collection.
Collect spheroids by centrifugation at 300 x g for 5 minutes at 20 °C.
Aspirate the supernatant with a pipette and add 50 μL of medium to the spheroids.
Resuspend spheroids gently by pipetting.
Add the spheroid mixture to the warm GelMA solution and mix gently by pipetting.
Maintain the spheroid concentration between 6340-12860 spheroids per mL of bioink for bioprinting.
Avoid higher concentrations as they easily cause blocking of the printing needle.
Add filter-sterilized photo-initiator Li-TPO-L stock solution in a final concentration of 2 mol% with respect to the number of double bonds and mix gently by pipetting.
Close the end of a sterile 3 cc cartridge with a tip cap (luer lock) and fill with bioink by pipetting.
Insert a plunger in the cartridge.
Hold the cartridge upside down and remove the tip cap, push the plunger toward the bioink until all air from the cartridge is removed.
Let the bioink cool down in the heating mantle of the bioprinter at 23 °C (20-30 min).
Screw in a pressure adapter on the top of the cartridge.
Close the clip on the inlet tube to prevent the bioink from leaking, mount a 22 G conical PE needle on the cartridge.
Install the cartridge in the heating mantle on the extrusion based printhead.
Plug the pressure inlet and open the clip on the inlet.
Load the G-code file of your design into the printing software.
Start needle length measurement.
Regulate the printing pressure by dispensing a little bioink in a sterile Petri dish.
Install a 6-well plate.
Open the well plate.
Close the hood.
Start printing.
Let the scaffolds be physically crosslinked for 10 min at 5 °C.
Irradiate the printed scaffolds for 60 s with a UV LED lamp (365 nm; 500 mW).
Add the corresponding growth media containing 100 U/mL of penicillin and 100 μg/mL of streptomycin to all wells with bioprinted grids.
Culture in a 37 °C CO2 incubator until you start microscopy.
Transfer a printed waffle grid into a microscopy dish.
Cover with imaging media.
Pre-coat sterile microscopy dishes with collagen IV and/or poly-D-lysine for spheroid attachment during live imaging analysis.
Supplement DMEM with sodium bicarbonate, HEPES-Na (pH 7.2), sodium pyruvate, L-glutamine, and glucose without phenol red for imaging medium preparation.
Prewarm the prepared imaging medium prior to use.
Gently wash out O2-probe pre-stained spheroids from agarose microwells using a 1 mL pipette while they float in media.
Transfer floating spheroids into a 15 mL conical bottom tube.
Rinse the well up to three times with an additional 1 mL of culture media and combine all spheroid suspensions in one vial.
Leave the vial vertically for up to 10 minutes to allow spheroids to settle and form a visible pellet at the bottom.
Carefully remove the media from the tube leaving the spheroids undisturbed.
Gently resuspend the spheroids in fresh culture medium sufficient for at least 20 spheroids per microscopy sample dish.
Attach the autoclavable silicon part of µ-chamber 12-well plate to the cover glass as a microscopy sample dish (24 x 60 mm, thickness #1).
Add an equal volume of spheroid suspension to each microscopy dish/well.
Incubate the dishes at 37 °C in a CO2 incubator for 1 hour to allow the spheroids to attach to the surface.
For oxygenation analysis coupled with other dyes, proceed with step 3.1.6.
For simple oxygenation analysis, proceed with step 3.1.7.
Carefully exchange the medium with one containing fluorescent probe(s) diluted to staining concentration and continue incubation for an additional 1 h to reach optimal intensity.
Aspirate the medium from the edges of the microscopy dishes using a 200 µL pipette.
Add imaging media sidewise in the microscopy dish without disturbing the spheroids.
Remove the medium from the microscopy dish.
Rinse once with imaging media.
Add the exact amount of imaging media to the sample (e.g., 300 µL per microwell).
Turn on the microscope and connected devices (i.e., excitation light source, camera, computer, incubator) 30 min before imaging.
Select excitation and emission filters for fluorescent or phosphorescent probes.
Choose exposure times for imaging.
Write automated measurement sequences for multi-parameter analyses.
Determine optimal imaging settings to minimize photobleaching.
Set up microscopy dish with stained spheroids on stage.
Preview sample in transmission light at low magnification objective.
Focus on spheroids and center them in image.
Bring the objective with the required high magnification to the working position.
Focus on transmission light mode in the middle (equatorial) cross-section of the spheroid.
Analyze similar cross-sections in and between groups, e.g., middle, top/bottom cross-sections of spheroids.
Apply the same chosen imaging settings of exposure time, excitation light source power, resolution, scan speed, and pinhole size for all measured objects in groups.
Merge intensity measurements of reference and sensitive channels of O2 probe using software function merge.
Collect images from the same optical section for reference and sensitive spectral channels of the O2 probe.
Use MMIR1 probe with red reference (excitation = 580 nm, emission = 650 nm) and near infrared O2-sensitive spectra (excitation = 635 nm, emission = 760 nm).
Repeat steps to collect a sufficient number of data points for statistical analysis.
Use time-lapse measurement mode for dynamic analysis of rapidly evolving cellular responses upon treatment with different drugs or compounds.
Perform measurements in imaging media at 37°C with periodic illumination of the sample.
Collect signals from fluorophores of interest, such as O2 probe reference and sensing channels, every 10 seconds for over 2 minutes.
Perform a focus check for every spheroid once periodic measurement is done.
Repeat focus check if required.
Proceed with step 3.3 for data analysis.
Open the .vsi file with O2-probe intensity data from reference and sensitive spectral channels made in merged mode.
Open the ratio analysis function window from the measure menu.
Choose the intensity of the reference channel as the numerator.
Choose the intensity of the sensitive channel as the denominator for R calculation.
Keep background settings for numerator and denominator intensities at 0.
Adjust scaling factor to ratio image until preview image provides desired resolution.
Apply adjusted scaling parameter equally to all spheroid images.
Set scaling parameter sufficiently high (at least 1,000) to ensure R image contains detailed information.
Press Apply to adjust parameters to the spheroid image.
Adjust brightness and contrast of the image in the adjust display window.
Manually determine linking and unlinking limits using fixed scaling option.
Determine range of false-color bar for R parameter presentation.
Ensure similar color bar range across all analytical samples for group comparisons.
Determine the spheroid diameter using the linear ruler function from the measure menu.
Export data as a spreadsheet table file.
Choose an ROI of required size and shape for analysis.
Apply the chosen ROI to both the periphery and hypoxic core of the spheroid.
Transform the ROI to the measurement object.
Analyze the average R inside the chosen ROI for peripheral and core measurements.
Export data in a spreadsheet-compatible table format.
Measure the diameters of spheroids using microscopy sections.
Record Rc and Rp values from each spheroid section.
Combine all recorded data into a single spreadsheet file.
Apply the same ROI coordinates to each image in time-lapse sets for analysis.
Express R parameters as percentages relative to the first cycle's R value.
Calculate the average R percentage from multiple ROIs for photobleaching analysis.
Assume negligible photobleaching if intensity decreases by less than 5% after 12 cycles.
Compare dynamic changes with a photobleaching curve control.
Calculate r, (Rp-Rc), and (Rp-Rc) / r for individual spheroids in the data set.
Analyze data distribution using Kolmogorov-Smirnov or relevant tests.
Choose appropriate statistical methods based on data normality.
Implement an independent t-test at p = 0.05 for comparison between groups.
